summary: 57 push-up repetitions completed across three clusters (42, 5, and 10 reps) separated by downward-dog pike rests. Depth is consistently excellent throughout, with the chest reaching near the floor on every rep. The three primary form faults are: (1) incomplete elbow lockout during the rapid-fire first 29 reps (pumping in the bottom half of the range of motion), (2) significant hip sag and lumbar hyperextension where the thighs/pelvis rest on the floor and the torso snakes upward, and (3) cervical hyperextension from craning the neck to look forward rather than keeping the gaze down with a neutral spine.
